source_text: Ἰακὼβ γεγονότας; Σαφὲς γὰρ ἂν γένοιτο καὶ λίαν ὡδὶ τὸ ἐν τῇ προσόδῳ παρηλλαγμένον. {ΠΑΛΛ.} Καὶ μάλα. {ΚΥΡ.} Ἔστι τοίνυν πρωτότοκος μὲν ὁ Ῥουβὴμ, ἐπ' αὐτῷ δὲ Συμεὼν, Λευὶ, καὶ Ἰούδας ἀπό γε μητρὸς τῆς Λείας. Βάλα δὲ αὖ τὸ θεραπαινίδιον τὸν Δάν τε καὶ Νεφθαλεὶμ, καὶ μὴν καὶ ἡ Ζελφὰ παιδίσκη Λείας, τὸν Γὰδ καὶ Ἀσὴρ, Λεία γε μὴν πρὸς τοῖς ἄλλοις τέσσαρσι, τὸν Ἰσάχαρ καὶ Ζαβουλὼν τίκτει· γενέσθην δὲ καὶ ἀπὸ Ῥαχὴλ Ἰωσὴφ καὶ Βενιαμίν. Οὐκοῦν πρῶτοι μὲν ἐκ Λείας, οἱ ἐξ ἐλευθέρας τέσσαρες, Ῥουβὴμ, καὶ Συμεὼν, Λευὶ καὶ Ἰούδας. Ἐκ δυοῖν δὲ θεραπαίναιν, Βάλας τε καὶ Ζελφᾶς, τέσσαρες, Δὰν καὶ Νεφθαλεὶμ, Γὰδ καὶ Ἀσήρ. Ἕτεροι δὲ αὖ ἐπὶ τούτοις τέσσαρες· δύο μὲν ἐκ Λείας, Ἰσάχαρ τε καὶ Ζαβουλὼν, ἀπὸ δέ γε τῆς Ῥαχὴλ, Ἰωσὴφ καὶ Βενιαμίν. Μεμνῆσθαι δὲ ἀναγκαῖον, ὡς εἰς δύο μεμέρισται φυλὰς ὁ Ἰωσὴφ κλῆρος, εἴς τε τὸν Ἐφραῒμ καὶ μέντοι τὸν Μανασσῆν, τοὺς ἐξ αὐτοῦ γεγονότας. {ΠΑΛΛ.} Συνίημι μὲν εὖ μάλα τῶν ὀνομάτων τὴν τάξιν· τί δ' ἂν εἴη λοιπὸν τὸ ζητούμενον ὡς ἔν γε δὴ τούτοις, σὸν ἤδη διατρανοῦν. {ΚΥΡ.} Προσιόντες, ὦ Παλλάδιε, τοῖς δώροις ἅμα, τοῦτο ἔδρων, οὐ καθ' ἡλικίαν, ἀλλὰ πρῶτος μὲν Ἰούδας, καίτοι τέταρτος ὢν κατὰ χρόνον, ἔννατος δὲ μετ' αὐτὸν Ἰσάχαρ, καὶ σὺν αὐτοῖς δέκατος Ζαβουλών. Συμμορία δὲ ὥσπερ μετὰ τούτους δευτέρα, Ῥουβὴμ ὁ πρωτότοκος, καὶ ὁ καθεξῆς καὶ δεύτερος, Συμεών. Συνῆπται δὲ καὶ ὁ Δὰν ἐκ δούλης. Καὶ πρός γε δὴ τούτοις, τάγμα τὸ τρίτον διὰ τριῶν ἐλευθέρων, Ἐφραΐμ τε καὶ Μανασσῆ καὶ Βενιαμίν. Συμμορία δὲ τετάρτη ἐν ἐσχάτοις, τῶν ἐκ θεραπαινῶν γεγονότων. Τρεῖς δὲ δὴ οὗτοι πάλιν, Δὰν καὶ Ἀσὴρ, καὶ Νεφθαλεὶμ, καίτοι προὔχοντες τῷ τῆς γενέσεως χρόνῳ, τῶν ὡς τάξει προτεταγμένων, Ἐφραΐμ τε, φημὶ, καὶ Μανασσῆ, καὶ Βενιαμίν. Ἆρ' οὐκ ἀναγκαίαν φῂς τὴν ἐπὶ τούτοις βάσανον; {ΠΑΛΛ.} Μάλιστά γε· τίς οὖν ὁ λόγος, πειρῶ μοι λέγειν. {ΚΥΡ.} Αἴνιγμά που τὸ χρῆμά ἐστι, καθάπερ ἐγᾦμαι πάλιν. Ὅτι τάξιν ἔχει τὴν πρώτην παρὰ Θεῷ τὰ διὰ Χριστοῦ τῶν ἐν νόμῳ· καὶ ὅτι τέθεινται μὲν οἱ πρῶτοι ἔσχατοι, οἱ δὲ ἔσχατοι πρῶτοι. Οἱ γὰρ ὡς ἐν χρόνῳ πρεσβύτεροι διά τε τοῦτο πρωτότοκοι, τοῦτ' ἔστιν ὁ Ἰσραὴλ, κατόπιν ἔρχεται τῶν ἐθνῶν. Καὶ οἱ τὸ δοῦλον ἔχοντες πνεῦμα, καὶ τῆς δουλευούσης Ἱερουσαλὴμ υἱοὶ, τὸ προὔχειν ἐν δόξῃ παραχωρήσουσι τοῖς τῆς ἐλευθέρας, ἥτις ἐστὶ μήτηρ ἡμῶν τῶν ἐν Χριστῷ δεδικαιωμένων, καὶ εἰς ἐλεύθερον ἀξίωμα κεκλημένων δι' ἐλευθέρου πνεύματος. Ὅρα γὰρ, εἰ δοκεῖ, τῶν θεωρημάτων τὸ ἀκριβές. Πρώτη μὲν γὰρ προσάγει τὸ δῶρον ἡ Ἰούδα φυλή· ἐξ ἧς ἀνέφυ κατὰ σάρκα Χριστός. Καὶ μετὰ ταύτην εὐθὺς ἡ Ἰσάχαρ τε καὶ Ζαβουλών· ἄμφω δὲ ἤσθην ἐλεύθεροι καὶ ἐξ ἐλευθέρων. Εἶτα Ῥουβὴμ ὁ πρω
pass_a_gloss: [completing Cyril’s question from §36: ‘those born of’] Jacob? For clear indeed would become very much in this way (ὡδί) the altered (παραλλάσσω) in the approach (πρόσοδος). PALL.: Very much so. CYR.: The firstborn (πρωτότοκος) then is Reuben, and after him Simeon, Levi and Judah, from the mother Leah. And again Bilhah the little servant (θεραπαινίδιον) [bore] Dan and Naphtali, and indeed Zilpah, Leah’s maid (παιδίσκη), Gad and Asher; and Leah, besides the other four, bears Issachar and Zebulun; and from Rachel came (dual γενέσθην) Joseph and Benjamin. So first from Leah, the four from the free woman (ἐλευθέρα): Reuben and Simeon, Levi and Judah. And from the two servant women (θεράπαιναι), Bilhah and Zilpah, four: Dan and Naphtali, Gad and Asher. And again others besides these, four: two from Leah, Issachar and Zebulun, and from Rachel, Joseph and Benjamin. And it is necessary to remember that the lot (κλῆρος) of Joseph has been divided into two tribes (φυλαί), into Ephraim and Manasseh, those born of him. PALL.: I understand very well the order (τάξις) of the names; but what the thing sought (τὸ ζητούμενον) may be in these, it is now yours to make clear (διατρανόω). CYR.: Approaching with the gifts, O Palladius, they did this: not according to age (ἡλικία), but first Judah, although being fourth according to time (χρόνος), and ninth after him Issachar, and with them tenth Zebulun. And a company (συμμορία) as it were second after these: Reuben the firstborn, and the next and second, Simeon. And Dan from a slave woman (δούλη) has been joined. And besides these a third rank (τάγμα) through three free-born: Ephraim and Manasseh and Benjamin. And a fourth company among the last (ἐν ἐσχάτοις), of those born from servant women. And these again three, Dan and Asher and Naphtali, although excelling (προέχω) in the time of birth those set before (προτάσσω) in order, I mean Ephraim and Manasseh and Benjamin. Do you not say the testing (βάσανος) upon these is necessary? PALL.: Most certainly; what then is the reason (λόγος), try to tell me. CYR.: The thing is somewhat a riddle (αἴνιγμα), as I think again: that the things through Christ have the first order with God compared with (genitive) those in the law; and that the first have been set last, and the last first. For those older in time and for this reason firstborn, that is Israel, come behind (κατόπιν) the nations (ἔθνη). And those having the slavish spirit (τὸ δοῦλον πνεῦμα), and sons of the Jerusalem that serves as a slave (δουλεύω), will yield (παραχωρέω) the excelling in glory to those of the free woman, who is mother of us, the justified in Christ, and called into free dignity (ἀξίωμα) through a free spirit (ἐλεύθερον πνεῦμα). See, if it seems good, the exactness (τὸ ἀκριβές) of the contemplations (θεωρήματα). For first the tribe of Judah brings the gift, from which Christ sprang up (ἀναφύω) according to flesh. And after this immediately that of Issachar and Zebulun; and both (dual ἤσθην) were free and from free. Then Reuben the first[-born]… [word divided; ‘-τότοκος’ opens §38]
pass_b_english: Cyril: …Jacob? For in this way the departure from that order in their approach would become very clear.

Cyril: Reuben, then, is the firstborn, and after him come Simeon, Levi and Judah, all from their mother Leah (Genesis 29:32–35). Bilhah, the servant girl, bore Dan and Naphtali (Genesis 30:4–8), and Zilpah, Leah’s maid, bore Gad and Asher (Genesis 30:9–13); and Leah, besides her other four, bore Issachar and Zebulun (Genesis 30:17–20). From Rachel, too, came Joseph and Benjamin (Genesis 30:22–24; 35:16–18). So the first are the four from Leah, the free woman: Reuben, Simeon, Levi and Judah. From the two servant women, Bilhah and Zilpah, come four: Dan and Naphtali, Gad and Asher. After these come another four: two from Leah, Issachar and Zebulun, and from Rachel, Joseph and Benjamin. We must also remember that Joseph’s lot was divided into two tribes, Ephraim and Manasseh, his sons (Genesis 48:5).
Palladius: I understand the order of the names very well. But it is now for you to make plain what, in all this, we are looking for.

Cyril: When they came forward with their gifts, Palladius, they did not come by age. First came Judah, though he was fourth in time (Numbers 7:12–17); after him Issachar, the ninth son, and with them Zebulun, the tenth (Numbers 7:18–29). After these came a second company, as it were: Reuben the firstborn, and Simeon, the next and second son (Numbers 7:30–41). Dan, a slave woman’s son, was joined to them as well. Next came a third rank, made up of three freeborn sons: Ephraim, Manasseh and Benjamin (Numbers 7:48–65). The fourth company, at the very end, is made up of those born of the servant women. These again are three, Dan, Asher and Naphtali (Numbers 7:66–83), although in the time of their birth they come before those placed ahead of them in order, I mean Ephraim, Manasseh and Benjamin. Would you not say this calls for close examination?
Palladius: Very much so. Try to tell me, then, what the reason is.

Cyril: The matter is a riddle, I think, once again. It shows that what comes through Christ holds the first rank with God over what belongs to the law, and that the first have been made last and the last first (Matthew 19:30). For those older in time, and for that reason firstborn, that is, Israel, come behind the Gentiles. And those who have the spirit of slavery (Romans 8:15), the sons of the Jerusalem that is in slavery, will yield the first place in glory to the sons of the free woman, who is the mother of us who have been justified in Christ (Galatians 4:25–26) and called to the dignity of the free through the Spirit of freedom. Look, if you will, at how exact these insights are. The tribe of Judah brings its gift first (Numbers 7:12), the tribe from which Christ sprang according to the flesh (Hebrews 7:14). Right after it come Issachar and Zebulun, both free and born of free parents. Then Reuben, the firstborn…

apparatus.note: PG OCR; column may cut mid-sentence.

Opens mid-question: §36 ends ‘τοὺς ἐξ’ and §37 begins ‘Ἰακὼβ γεγονότας;’, so the English opens ‘…Jacob?’. Birth order as Cyril gives it matches Genesis: Reuben 1, Simeon 2, Levi 3, Judah 4 (Leah, Genesis 29:32–35); Dan 5, Naphtali 6 (Bilhah, Genesis 30:4–8); Gad 7, Asher 8 (Zilpah, Genesis 30:9–13); Issachar 9, Zebulun 10 (Leah, Genesis 30:17–20); Joseph 11 (Genesis 30:22–24) and Benjamin 12 (Genesis 35:16–18) from Rachel. Joseph’s two tribes: Genesis 48:5 (also Joshua 14:4). Order of the gifts in Numbers 7: Judah day 1 (7:12), Issachar 2 (7:18), Zebulun 3 (7:24), Reuben 4 (7:30), Simeon 5 (7:36), Gad 6 (7:42), Ephraim 7 (7:48), Manasseh 8 (7:54), Benjamin 9 (7:60), Dan 10 (7:66), Asher 11 (7:72), Naphtali 12 (7:78). TEXTUAL FLAG: in the second company the Greek reads ‘Συνῆπται δὲ καὶ ὁ Δὰν ἐκ δούλης’ (‘Dan, a slave woman’s son, was joined to them’), but Numbers 7:42 has Gad on the sixth day, Dan appears again in the fourth company in this same section, and §38 names Gad (‘Συμεών τε καὶ Γὰδ, ὅς ἐστιν ἐκ δούλης’). Δάν is a slip, Cyril’s or a copyist’s, for Γάδ. Pass B translates the Greek as it stands; the editor may wish to print ‘Gad’ with a note. For that reason the second company is cited Numbers 7:30–41 only (Reuben and Simeon), and Gad’s day 7:42–47 is not cited here. ‘The first have been made last and the last first’ cited to Matthew 19:30 (‘many who are first will be last, and the last first’), whose order matches; Matthew 20:16 and Mark 10:31 are parallels. ‘The spirit of slavery’ cited to Romans 8:15 (πνεῦμα δουλείας). ‘The Jerusalem that is in slavery… the free woman, who is the mother of us’ is Galatians 4:25–26 (‘she is in slavery with her children… the Jerusalem above is free, and she is our mother’). δι’ ἐλευθέρου πνεύματος rendered ‘through the Spirit of freedom’ with a capital (cf. 2 Corinthians 3:17, uncited), since it answers the Spirit of adoption of Romans 8:15; a lower-case ‘a spirit of freedom’ is possible, and the reading is doubtful, so no citation. ‘From which Christ sprang according to the flesh’ cited to Hebrews 7:14 (‘our Lord sprang from Judah’); cf. Romans 9:5 for ‘according to the flesh’. The section ends in the middle of the word πρωτότοκος (‘πρω-’ / ‘-τότοκος’); the whole word ‘firstborn’ is placed here, so §38 should open ‘…Simeon and Gad’.
